name: Automotive Service Technician
description: Automotive service technicians diagnose and repair cars and light trucks — and diagnosis is the part that pays, because a modern vehicle is a network of computers. ⚠ 805,600 people do this work nationally with about 70,000 openings a year, and Florida teaches it at technical colleges in 150-hour blocks you can stop and start.
credentialNote: ⚠ No state licence stands between you and this work — Florida licenses the SHOP, not the technician: anyone paid to repair other people's vehicles must register the business with FDACS under the Florida Motor Vehicle Repair Act. ⚠⚠ But two credentials matter. FEDERAL LAW requires EPA Section 609 certification of anyone who services vehicle air conditioning for payment. And ASE certification is the currency of the trade: the tests need two years of hands-on experience, of which a relevant training programme can replace one. ⚠⚠⚠ On the education side the requirement runs the other way — Florida Statute 1004.925 requires every automotive service technology education PROGRAMME in the state to be industry certified. Ask to see it before you enrol.
bodyHtml:
What the work actually is

O*NET: diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul automotive vehicles. The task statements are the job — test drive vehicles and test components and systems, using equipment such as infrared engine analyzers, compression gauges and computerized diagnostic devices; troubleshoot fuel, ignition and emissions control systems using electronic testing equipment; repair, reline, replace and adjust brakes; perform routine and scheduled maintenance services; confer with customers to obtain descriptions of vehicle problems and to discuss work to be performed.

⚠ Note the first and the last. The work is diagnosis before it is repair — a modern car is a network of computers, and the skill that pays is working out what is actually wrong. And the customer conversation is part of the job: explaining a fault and its cost to someone who did not want to be there is a skill shops hire and promote for.

Projected need

O*NET, on federal projections: 805,600 automotive service technicians and mechanics employed (2024), growth “average (3% to 4%)”, and ⚠ 70,000 openings a year. Median wages $50,620 (2025) ($24.34 an hour).

⚠ Read the openings figure rather than the growth figure. The occupation is not expanding quickly, but it is enormous and constantly replacing people — 70,000 openings a year against 23,000 materials engineers employed in the whole country. On education, O*NET's respondents split 32% post-secondary certificate, 30% less than high school, 26% high school or equivalent: ⚠ you can get in without training, and the certificate is what separates the people who advance from the people who stay on lube and tyres.

⚠⚠ Where this is actually taught — and it is not where the rest of this site looks

56 Florida public institutions award a vehicle maintenance credential and 47 of them award in automotive specifically — one of the widest footprints of any programme on this site. ⚠ But almost all of them are district technical colleges: Atlantic, Lake, Sheridan, Traviss, Lindsey Hopkins, Erwin, McFatter, Withlacoochee and thirty more. Only a handful of state colleges carry it.

⚠ That has a consequence for how you search. A technical college is a public institution, it is usually the cheapest route there is, and its programmes are on the state framework — but it is not a university, it does not award a degree, and it will not appear in a search for one. Look for your county's technical college by name.

⚠⚠ It had a consequence for this site too, and it is worth saying plainly: until this path was written, floridacourserepo.com carried no technical colleges at all — 39 institutions, every one a state college or university. Thirty-five were added to publish this page.

⚠⚠⚠ The structure to understand before you enrol: nine exits, not one finish line

Florida's framework is Master Automotive Service Technology, 1,800 hours, nine occupational completion points. Each OCP is a complete, hireable qualification on its own — and the hours below are the state's, not an estimate:

  • A — Automotive Services Assistor (300 hours). The entry point, and the state recommends completing it first; after that the order is up to the instructor.
  • B — Engine Repair · C — Automatic Transmission and Transaxle · D — Manual Drivetrain and Axle · E — Suspension and Steering · F — Brakes · H — Heating and Air Conditioning (150 hours each).
  • G — Electrical and Electronic Systems · I — Engine Performance (300 hours each). ⚠ These two are the diagnostic core and they are where the money is.

⚠ You can stop at a completion point, go to work, and come back. That is what the structure is for, and it is the single most useful thing to know about this programme. A shorter Maintenance and Light Repair certificate (600 hours) exists for the fastest route into paid work.

⚠ The OCP letters line up with the ASE certification areas (A1 through A8), which is deliberate: the framework marks its ASE tasks explicitly, so the coursework is written against the certification you will later sit.

Necessary skills

  • Diagnosis — the skill the trade pays for. Reading live data, following a circuit, forming a hypothesis and testing it. Parts-swapping is what the job looks like from outside; diagnosis is what it is.
  • Electrical and electronics. ⚠ The two longest OCPs are electrical systems and engine performance for a reason — nearly every modern complaint touches a sensor, a module or a network.
  • Hand skills and care with other people's property. Torque specs, fasteners, fluids, and the habit of not damaging what you are working on.
  • Customer communication. Explaining a fault and a price is a paid skill, and it is the route to service advisor and service manager.
  • Continuous retraining. Hybrids, high-voltage systems and driver-assistance recalibration are current, not future. ⚠ A technician who stops learning becomes a technician who only does brakes.

Advice

  • ⚠⚠ Ask any programme to show you its industry certification. Florida Statute 1004.925 requires every automotive service technology education programme in the state to be industry certified — ASE Education Foundation certification is what that means in practice. It is the law, and it is a fair question to ask on a tour.
  • Get EPA Section 609 before you touch air conditioning. Federal law: anyone who services a motor vehicle air conditioning system for consideration must be trained and certified under an EPA-approved programme. It is cheap, it is quick, and it is not optional.
  • Plan for ASE certification, and know the rule: the tests need two years of hands-on experience, and a relevant training programme can substitute for one of them — so starting the certificate early shortens the road.
  • ⚠ Budget for tools. Most shops expect a technician to own their hand tools, and building a set is a real and continuing expense that nobody mentions in a brochure. Ask what the programme expects you to buy, and what an employer supplies.
  • Dealer programmes are a real route — several Florida colleges run manufacturer-specific training with a sponsoring dealership, which pairs classroom terms with paid work. Ask whether the college has one and what the commitment is.
  • ⚠ If you want to run the shop rather than work in it, the associate degree in automotive service management technology is the step above these certificates, and the certificates count toward it at several colleges.

programs.note: The programme itself — 47 Florida public institutions award in it, and ⚠ the great majority are district technical colleges. The programme page lists them, which is the quickest way to find the one nearest you.

⚠ The step ABOVE the bay rather than a route into it: the associate degree in automotive service management technology is filed here, and it is how technicians move toward service management, warranty work or teaching.

sources.label: ASE Education Foundation
sources.note: The body that accredits automotive training programmes — what Florida's statutory certification requirement means in practice.

sources.label: EPA — Section 609 technician training and certification
sources.note: ⚠ *“Any person who repairs or services a motor vehicle air conditioning system for consideration … must be properly trained and certified”* under an EPA-approved programme.

sources.note: ⚠ Florida registers the SHOP, not the technician: anyone paid to repair other people's vehicles must register with the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services under the Florida Motor Vehicle Repair Act (ss. 559.901–559.9221, F.S.). Worth knowing before you open your own.
